Theorem
[Marcinkiewicz interpolation] 1. ch9:9.8\group chapter-9Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0240 Let $1\le q<r<\infty $, and let $T$ map $L^q(\Omega )\cap L^r(\Omega )$ linearly into itself. Suppose \begin{equation} \tag {9.24} \mu _{Tf}(t)\le \left(\frac{T_1\| f\| _q}{t}\right)^q, \qquad \mu _{Tf}(t)\le \left(\frac{T_2\| f\| _r}{t}\right)^r \end{equation} for every $f$ in that intersection and $t>0$. If $q<p<r$ and \[ \frac1p=\frac\alpha q+\frac{1-\alpha }r, \] then $T$ extends boundedly to $L^p(\Omega )$ and \begin{equation} \tag {9.25} \| Tf\| _p\le C T_1^\alpha T_2^{1-\alpha }\| f\| _p, \end{equation} where $C=C(p,q,r)$.
Proof

\sketch Split $f=f_1+f_2$ at the level $s$, with $f_1$ supported where $|f|>s$. Linearity and (9.24) bound $\mu _{Tf}(t)$ by the weak estimates for $f_1$ and $f_2$. Insert this bound into (9.23), choose $t=As$, and use Fubini to obtain

\[ \| Tf\| _p^p\le C\left(T_1^qA^{p-q}+T_2^rA^{p-r}\right)\| f\| _p^p. \]

Balancing the two terms in $A$ gives (9.25); density gives the extension.

□
